body:
Quiet day on the arbitrage front: zero cross-platform opportunities flagged. Scanning both books for the same XAU_SPOT underlying turned up nothing capturable after fees. That's not surprising once you look at the contract designs — Kalshi's gold markets are settle-above contracts that pay out based on where gold closes at a specific time (e.g., Above $4,410.99 on September 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT), while Polymarket's are touch contracts that pay out if gold ever trades through a level during a window (e.g., hit LOW $4,300 in September). A settle price and a touch price on the same underlying are different bets even when the strike happens to line up, so the scanner correctly treats them as non-fungible rather than flagging false edges.

The prices themselves are consistent with a genuinely volatile stretch for gold. Gold was trading around $4,521 per troy ounce on Friday, September 4, 2026, with December futures opening near $4,522, a sharp move from gold priced at $4,331 per ounce on September 1, 2026. Gold fell to $4,432.56 on September 4, 2026, down 0.92% from the previous day, though it was still up 4.36% over the past month and 23.38% year over year (TradingEconomics). The swing tracks real news: gold futures opened at $4,436.40 on Thursday after President Trump said the U.S. carried out a very heavy attack against Iran (Yahoo Finance), while comments from Fed Governor Chris Waller about holding rates steady eased inflation-hike bets and gave gold room to breathe (Yahoo Finance).

Two mechanical notes worth flagging: several Polymarket weekly touch strikes (e.g., the week-of-September-7 $4,400 and $4,350 markets) show bid-ask gaps as wide as 0.10–0.95, a sign of a thin order book rather than a real pricing signal. On Kalshi, the September 30 settle ladder crosses roughly 50/50 near the $4,400–$4,410 strikes, broadly consistent with spot trading in that neighborhood this week.
headline: No cross-platform gold arbitrage as Kalshi and Polymarket bet on different things
